ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: Figure 2 is a schematic map of the distribution of crops in India. The legend on the right marks four crop symbols: × represents jute, the circular symbol represents cotton, the small tree/tea plant-like symbol represents tea, and the forked symbol represents sugarcane. In the figure, × is mainly concentrated in northeastern India and near the Ganges Delta; cotton symbols mostly fall in western India, the Deccan Plateau, and the interior of the peninsula; sugarcane symbols are mainly distributed in the northern Ganges Plain area; tea symbols, however, are marked in the central-eastern, relatively inland area of India, rather than being obviously concentrated in northeastern Assam-Darjeeling area or the southern mountains. Then reason: India's main jute producing area is near the Ganges Delta, and the figure is basically consistent; the main cotton producing areas are in the Deccan Plateau, the west, and the central region, and the figure is generally consistent; sugarcane is mostly distributed in irrigated agricultural areas such as the Ganges Plain, and the figure is also basically consistent; tea is actually mainly distributed in northeastern Assam, Darjeeling, and the southern mountains, while the tea marked positions in the figure deviate from these typical producing areas, so the one obviously inconsistent with the actual distribution is tea.
